questionText: Company Apex #19 forfeited 560 shares of Rs. 10 each on which Rs. 7 per share was received. 280 of these shares were reissued as fully paid-up at Rs. 8 per share. What amount is transferred to Capital Reserve Account?

options.text: Share Forfeiture Dr. Rs. 1,400 to Capital Reserve A/c Rs. 1,400
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Forfeiture and Reissue of Shares: Transfer to Capital Reserve.

options.text: Share Forfeiture Dr. Rs. 1,960 to Capital Reserve A/c Rs. 1,960
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Share Forfeiture Dr. Rs. 560 to Capital Reserve A/c Rs. 560
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Share Forfeiture Dr. Rs. 3,920 to Capital Reserve A/c Rs. 3,920
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Company Accounts: Accounting for Share and Debenture Capital (Forfeiture and Reissue of Shares: Transfer to Capital Reserve):
Share Forfeiture Dr. Rs. 1,400 to Capital Reserve A/c Rs. 1,400

Detailed Context:
1. Forfeited amount on 560 shares = 560 x Rs. 7 = Rs. 3,920.
2. Forfeited amount proportional to 280 reissued shares = 280 x Rs. 7 = Rs. 1,960.
3. Discount allowed on reissue = 280 x (Rs. 10 - Rs. 8) = Rs. 560.
4. Net gain transferred to Capital Reserve = Rs. 1,960 - Rs. 560 = Rs. 1,400.
Hence Option D is correct.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.

premium. Money is receivable as follows:
Application = 40 (including premium)
Allotment=45
 
First and Final call = Remaining amount
The public applied for 50,000 shares. The company rejected application for
10,000 shares and made a pro rata allotment to the rest of the applicants. A
shareholder applying for 400 shares, didn't pay the allotment and call
money and his allotted shares were forfeited by the company. Later, the
forfeited shares were reissued at 80 each as fully paid.

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

detailedSolution:

4. Call arrears: 300 * 25 = Rs. 7,500.
5. Total credited to Calls-in-Arrears = 9,500 + 7,500 = Rs. 17,000.
6. Matches Option C.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.
